You are a senior numerical test engineer on treams-rs (T-matrix scattering: Rust core crates/treams-core, PyO3 bindings, Python API python/treams_rs, pytest+Hypothesis tests/, Rust proptests). Work ONLY in the git worktree lanes/flaky (branch lane-flaky at 127d24c (condensed into 8251007)). Time limit: 90 minutes of wall time; commit and report within it.

TASK: four pre-existing tests fail on rare random draws, which makes CI nondeterministic. For each: reproduce, find out WHY it fails (rounding floor of the quantity vs a tolerance that does not scale with it; an ill-conditioned input region; or a real bug), and fix it properly:

  • If the discrepancy is rounding, replace the fixed tolerance with one derived from the rounding floor of the compared quantity (e.g. a few ulps of the sum of term moduli, of |a|^T|T||a|, of the condition-scaled magnitude), with the constant justified by a calibration over many random draws (report the worst observed / floor ratio), keeping the relative tolerance itself. Never just loosen a tolerance by a factor; never shrink the strategy to hide a legitimate region.
  • If it is an ill-conditioned region where the checked identity itself loses digits, bound the check by that conditioning (documented) or exclude the region only if the identity is meaningless there, and say so.
  • If it is a real bug (wrong result beyond rounding), stop and report it precisely (reproducer, expected vs actual) instead of hiding it; fix it only if the fix is small and clearly right, with a test. Record each failing input as a deterministic regression (proptest-regressions entry committed, or a Hypothesis @example) so the case replays forever.

THE FOUR TESTS:

  1. Rust proptest angular::tests::angular_functions_match_legendre_and_ignore_the_length_unit (crates/treams-core/src/angular.rs) failed once: 1.86e-12 against its tolerance. The seed was not recorded: run it many times with PROPTEST_CASES raised and PROPTEST_DISABLE_FAILURE_PERSISTENCE unset to capture a seed.
  2. A Hypothesis property failed with order=4, x=0.31478578000682234, singular=True, helicity=True, chiral=False: the third gradient differs by 3.64e-12 absolute (8.5e-13 relative) against rtol=atol=2e-13. Find which test draws (order, x, singular, helicity, chiral) -- grep tests/ for a @given with those argument names (likely polar/vector-wave translation adjoint tests) -- and reproduce with @example.
  3. tests/test_fields.py::test_cylindrical_polarization_pair_permutation
  4. tests/test_geometry_misc.py::test_skew_diffraction_pairs_and_plane_basis For 3 and 4 a Hypothesis database holding their failing examples is at py_hypothesis_db (copy it to .hypothesis and run wt.sh pytest tests/test_fields.py::... without -p no:cacheprovider interfering with the DB; Hypothesis replays stored examples from .hypothesis/examples). Print the failing example and error.

TOOLS: every Bash call starts in a fresh shell: cd lanes/flaky && .... scratch: wt.sh build-ext | rust-test [filter] | rust-lint | rust-fmt | pytest <args> | py-fmt | py-lint | py-types | gates | full | parity | rust-doc. Shared venv .venv (never install anything). Other engineers use the machine (4 CPUs). Rust tests: PYO3_PYTHON=.venv/bin/python cargo test --locked -p treams-core --lib <name> works too. RULES: change tests only (unless a real bug is found); keep category markers; strict lints (clippy all+pedantic+nursery -D warnings; ruff; pyrefly). Small signed commits (automatic signing, never disable), conventional subject, body with the cause, the calibration numbers and the pinned example, ending with exactly: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com Claude-Session: [link to a conversation in the cloud] Use git commit -F <file under scratch>. At the end: wt.sh full (parity step shows exactly two known failures: wigner3j_large_j100_30_m99_-30 and diff_lattice_sum sw1.* -- anything else is yours), repeat each fixed test at least 20 times with fresh seeds (Rust: PROPTEST_DISABLE_FAILURE_PERSISTENCE=1 loops; Hypothesis: --hypothesis-seed=1..20 and HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=thorough once), clean git status. REPORT: per test the cause, fix, calibration, pinned example, commit sha, and the repeat-run results.

All four flaky tests are fixed in lanes/flaky (branch lane-flaky), in three signed commits on top of 127d24c (condensed into 8251007). Only tests changed. None of the failures was a real bug. Tests 2 and 3 turned out to be the same failure: the stored database example for test 3 is exactly the input given for test 2.

wt.sh full passes gates and the full Python suite (4521 passed, 36 skipped). Parity shows only the two known failures (wigner3j_large_j100_30_m99_-30 and diff_lattice_sum sw1.*). git status is clean; .hypothesis/ is gitignored.

Test 1 — Rust angular proptest (commit e8afebe (condensed into 8251007))

  • Reproduction: with PROPTEST_CASES=300000 it failed after 203,932 cases and shrank to (l,m)=(1,1), θ=3.1415779067281138 (1.47e-5 from the south pole), φ=0, radius=0.1, exponent=0. Distance was 3.71e-12 against a tolerance of 2.00e-12, on the first (Legendre) assertion.
  • Cause (ill-conditioned input, not a bug): the Legendre reference only receives z = fl(cos θ).
    • Near a pole, rounding cos θ shifts the angle the reference sees by up to about eps/(4 sin θ), and below θ ≈ 1e-8 it loses θ entirely.
    • The value then moves by that shift times the tangential gradient. That breaks the tolerance of 1e-12·(|value|+tangent), which is 4504 eps, whenever sin θ is below about 5e-5.
    • The Cartesian side is accurate.
  • Fix:
    • A new helper check_legendre evaluates the Cartesian side in the direction z actually represents, with sine sqrt((1−z)(1+z)) accurate to ulps. The tolerance is unchanged.
    • The length-unit checks still run at the drawn θ, so near-pole Cartesian evaluations stay covered.
    • I added a property, angular_functions_match_legendre_near_the_poles, that draws θ within 1e-12 to 0.1 of either pole. Uniform draws land there only about once in 10,000 cases.
    • I tried adding a conditioning term to the tolerance but dropped it: it made the check as loose as about 1e-4 relative near the poles.
  • Calibration (error / (eps·(|value|+tangent)), 1e6 cases per property): worst 512 in both, at 1−|z| = 7.5e-9, against 4504 allowed. That residue comes from the reference's own rounding of 1−z², which analysis bounds at about 1024.
  • Pinned: crates/treams-core/proptest-regressions/angular.txt, entry cc 5ae68412…. It fails on the old binary and passes on the new one.

Tests 2 and 3 — tests/test_fields.py::test_cylindrical_polarization_pair_permutation (commit 2b0ea64 (condensed into 8251007))

  • Reproduction: the database example is order=4, x=0.31478578000682234, singular=True, helicity=True, chiral=False. The origin cotangent (the third gradient) is [1.7e4, −4.27, −114.6], and its −4.27 entry differs by 3.64e-12 (8.5e-13 relative) against rtol=atol=2e-13.
  • Cause (rounding): permuting the modes reorders the sums over modes. The terms reach about 1e4 because outgoing waves near the axis are large. The coefficient and ks cotangents agree bit for bit.
  • Fix:
    • A new helper _mode_sum_floors sums, per compared entry, the moduli of the per-mode, per-point terms, using single-mode, single-point field evaluations and their pullbacks.
    • The bound is 2e-13*|expected| + 16*eps*floor, keeping rtol 2e-13. It is checked with assert_array_less, because assert_allclose rejects an array atol.
  • Calibration over 3e4 random draws (worst error / (eps·floor)): field 1.72, point cotangents 4.70, origin cotangents 3.29, coefficient and ks cotangents 0. The old tolerance was exceeded by up to 4.1× on the origin cotangents; the failing case itself uses 0.25 of its floor.
  • Pinned: @example(order=4, x=0.31478578000682234, singular=True, helicity=True, chiral=False).

Test 4 — tests/test_geometry_misc.py::test_skew_diffraction_pairs_and_plane_basis (commit 7320d85 (condensed into 8251007))

  • Reproduction: shear=1.6, radius=2.6 gives a shape mismatch, 19 orders against 21, so this was not a tolerance failure.
  • Cause (ill-conditioned boundary region): the orders (1,−4) and (−1,4) have length exactly 2.6. The basis enumerates the reciprocal of a = reciprocal(b), which equals b only to rounding, so rounding decides whether those orders are kept. Here b keeps them and reciprocal(a) drops them. The comparison is meaningless for such orders; the binding is correct.
  • Fix:
    • The test enumerates the orders of the lattice the basis holds (basis.lattice.reciprocal).
    • Any order where the two enumerations disagree must lie on the cutoff to within 4 ulps of |n||b|.
    • Components must match within rtol 1e-7 (the default, kept) plus 4 eps·(|q|+|n||b|), replacing the fixed atol 2e-14.
  • Calibration:
    • 2e4 uniform draws never hit the cutoff; the worst component error was 1.45 ulps of the floor.
    • I also ran all 29,170 shear/radius combinations on grids of 1/8, 1/10, 1/20 and 1/25. The enumerations disagreed on 26 of them, and every disagreeing order sat exactly on the cutoff (distance 0). Components stayed within 1.18 ulps of the floor.
  • Pinned: @example(shear=1.6, radius=2.6).

Repeat runs, all passing:

  • Rust: 20 runs of both angular properties with PROPTEST_DISABLE_FAILURE_PERSISTENCE=1, plus one run of 200,000 cases each. The pinned seed replays and passes.
  • Python: both tests passed with --hypothesis-seed 1 to 20, and once with HYPOTHESIS_PROFILE=thorough. Test 4 has its own @settings(max_examples=35), so the thorough profile runs 35 examples for it and 300 for the field test.

The calibration scripts (not committed) are in scratch as cal23.py, cal4.py and cal4b.py.
